item.title: Remembering Harry Haun, Who Bore Witness to Broadway with Wit and Wonder
item.description: Connections forged over five decades gave him insider access to everyone from Jessica Chastain and Harvey Fierstein to the late Broadway publicist Susan Schulman and the legendary Lynne Meadow.

item.title: Oscar Murillo Reflects On Building a Body of Work That Resists Linear Time
item.description: The artist frames his practice as a form of sedimentation, where ideas, marks and social encounters coexist across different temporal speeds.

item.title: Miami’s Sushi Scene Is Having a Moment
item.description: An influx of omakase counters, Michelin stars and Tokyo-trained chefs is elevating Miami's sushi scene.

item.title: Painter Helene Schjerfbeck’s Life in Layers at the Met
item.description: The silence in her work is tender, delicate and fierce all at once. In a world dominated by men, despite isolation, illness and self-doubt, she carved out her space.

item.title: Celebrating the Power of Film and the Best of Humanity at Park City’s Last Sundance
item.description: Despite the sentimentality that covered Park City more heartily than the snow, films like 'The Friend’s House Is Here' reminded us how remarkable good movies can be at capturing our better impulses.

item.title: Dominique Ansel’s Beauty-Driven Approach to Pastry
item.description: Now, the famed pastry chef is gearing up for the debut of a new linzer cookie inspired by nail polish colors.

item.title: Sara Hooker Raises $50M to Challenge A.I.’s Conventional Wisdom
item.description: Sara Hooker’s new startup Adaption Labs is challenging A.I.’s reliance on massive data and compute power with adaptive, real-time learning.

item.title: In L.A., Julia Stoschek’s Art Collection Activates a Cinema Landmark
item.description: Observer spoke to curator Udo Kittelmann about willfully modifying art world terminology, being firmly anti-black box and the unmistakable constancy of human desires.

item.title: Sam Altman and Dario Amodei Clash Over Ads and the Future of A.I.
item.description: What started as a technical arms race between Sam Altman and Dario Amodei has evolved into a public feud over narrative control.

item.title: With “Happy Zoo,” Anita Lam Makes a Case for Artistic Environmentalism
item.description: Lam’s curatorial work sits at the intersection of art, ecology, technology and philosophy, but far from being preachy or pessimistic, her approach is playful and, at times, mischievous.
